children.text: An approximately 800m beach in Barangay Yapak at the northern tip of Boracay, known for coarse sand mixed with broken shells and deep turquoise water. It is 15–20 minutes from White Beach by e-trike and free to enter, making it a good half-day escape from the crowded beaches.
Puka Shell Beach stretches for about

along the coast of Barangay Yapak at the northern tip of Boracay Island. Where White Beach on the island's west side has sand as fine as flour, the sand here is mixed with fragments of shells broken by the waves, so the grains are coarse and crunch under your feet. Just a few steps from the water's edge the sea gets deep, so the color changes quickly from jade green to deep navy, and both ends of the beach are closed off by rocky headlands covered in forest. Because the beach faces north, on clear days you can see the ridge of Carabao Island in Romblon province across the sea on the horizon.

The name comes from the puka shells that were once common on this beach. Puka means "hole" in Hawaiian and refers to bead-like pieces of cone snail shell whose tip has been worn down by waves and coral rubble until a hole forms through the middle; string them together and you have a necklace. Old photos show that around
the 1970s

, when puka shell jewelry was in fashion, people who came to collect the shells camped on the beach in tents, and the sign at the entrance still says this is the place that first made Boracay known to the world. Because of overcollection, intact puka shells are now hard to find, and the beach is also called Yapak Beach after its barangay.
In
March 2018

, just before the whole island was rehabilitated, local media reported that the Malay municipal government demolished about 30 souvenir stalls and snack shops that had violated easement and sanitation rules, saying it wanted to restore the beach to its original state. There is still no lodging on the beach itself, and the facilities consist of little more than souvenir stalls and simple eateries near the entrance and huts for rent. However, in
July 2025
Singapore's I'M Hotel Group announced that it would build a 381-room resort, I'Msignia, on this beach, and according to industry news in
July 2026
its soft opening has been pushed back to
. The atmosphere of the beach may change once the resort opens, so check the latest news.

It suits travelers who want to slip away from the crowds and music of White Beach to a quiet stretch of sea, and couples who want to spend a relaxed half day taking photos. On the other hand, since the water deepens quickly and the waves are often strong, White Beach is easier for playing in shallow water with small children or for anyone who is not a confident swimmer. Boracay's island entry procedures and general travel information are covered separately in the
Boracay
entry.

blocks.title: Walk on sand full of shell fragments

children.text: Scoop up a handful of sand and you will see bits of shell glinting among the white coral grains. Walking slowly from one end of the beach to the other and back takes about
30–40 minutes
. Look at the sand and shells, but do not take any with you.

Because the beach faces north, on clear days Carabao Island lies long and low on the horizon across the sea. Head to the rocks at either end of the beach to fit the white sand and the island into one frame, but the rocks are slippery and sharp, so wear sneakers or water shoes.

blocks.title: Rest in the shade of a hut

children.text: Stalls near the entrance rent out thatched huts and sun loungers. Some will give you a spot if you order drinks, so ask about the price and conditions first. Most of the beach has no shade, so a spot like this is essential at midday.

Near the rocks at both ends of the beach the water is clear and small tropical fish gather, making it a good spot for casual snorkeling. It is not a famous snorkeling site, so bring your own mask, and on days with waves keep your distance so you are not pushed against the rocks.

blocks.title: Browse shell jewelry at the entrance stalls

children.text: The path to the beach entrance is lined with stalls selling shell necklaces and bracelets, hats, and sarongs. Buying souvenirs here instead of picking up shells on the beach also keeps you within the rules. Prices are negotiable, and many stalls accept cash only.

blocks.title: A rest stop for island-hopping bangkas

children.text: Many Boracay island-hopping tours, along with Crystal Cove Island and a snorkeling spot, pull up at Puka Shell Beach so guests can swim and rest for a while. If getting there by road seems like a hassle, check that Puka Shell Beach is included in the tour before you book.
Arrive before
or after
4 PM
and the sun is less harsh and there are fewer people. At sunset you can watch the sky and sea turn red far more peacefully than at White Beach.

blocks.title: Kayaking and paddleboarding on calm days

children.text: In peak season, kayaks and paddleboards are sometimes available for rent near the entrance. Calm mornings are best, and since wind can easily push you out to sea, stay close to the shoreline.

After dark, fewer drivers wait for passengers at the entrance, so it can be hard to find a ride back. Book a round-trip charter when you go, or get the driver's phone number.

Stops and their order vary by tour, and on rough days Puka Shell Beach is sometimes skipped. Time on the beach tends to be short, so if you want to rest here for long, it is better to come separately by road.
Flights from Manila to Caticlan Airport (MPH) take about
1 hour
, and from the airport it is a
7–10-minute
tricycle ride to Caticlan Jetty Port, where boats leave for Boracay. There are also direct flights from Clark to Caticlan, taking about
1 hour 15 minutes
Kalibo International Airport (KLO) is about
68km
by road from the jetty port, so you need another
1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours
by van or bus, at about
per person. Scheduled direct flights from Incheon arrive at Kalibo.
From Caticlan Jetty Port to Boracay's Cagban Port takes about
15 minutes
by bangka. You pay a boat fare of

Since
December 19, 2024

, the Aklan provincial government has run Boracay iPass, an integrated ticketing system for paying these fees in one go. You can pay online in advance and keep the QR code, or pay at the port counter; fees and procedures may change, so check the latest announcements.
During the southwest monsoon season (
June–October
), boats sometimes dock at Tambisaan Port on the island's east side to avoid the waves. To go straight from the port to Puka Shell Beach, a shared e-trike costs about
per person and a charter about
per vehicle.
From White Beach, head north along the island's central main road for about
15–20 minutes
to reach the beach entrance. Most tricycles on the island are electric e-trikes.
A shared ride costs about
per person, but you may have to wait until the seats fill up, or get off on the main road and walk in for about
10 minutes
A charter costs about

per vehicle depending on where you start. There are no meters, so agree on the fare before you ride. Some drivers wait for passengers at the entrance, but there are fewer from late afternoon, so it is easier to ask your driver to wait or to agree on a round-trip fare.
A half-day join tour by bangka around Crystal Cove Island, Magic Island, a snorkeling spot, and Puka Shell Beach costs about

1–2 PM
Some packages leave out the Crystal Cove and Magic Island entrance fees (about
each), so check what's included and whether the tour stops at Puka Shell Beach.
You can also rent an e-trike by the hour for a land tour that combines Puka Shell Beach with sights in the north and east of the island. It costs about
per hour per vehicle (up to 4 people); book at least 2 hours if you want enough time on the beach.
The best time to visit Puka Shell Beach is the
November–May
dry season. There is little rain and the sky is clear, so the water is at its most beautiful, and
December–April
in particular brings relatively gentle winds and clear water, ideal for walks and photos.
March–May
is almost rain-free, but midday temperatures climb to around
and there is little shade on the beach, so go early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
June–October

is the rainy season of the southwest monsoon (habagat), with frequent rain, and on many days big waves roll onto Puka Shell Beach, making swimming difficult. Island-hopping routes also change or are canceled depending on sea conditions, and in
July–October
typhoons can cancel flights and boats.
Typhoons can pass even in the dry season. In
November 2025

, Typhoons Tino and Uwan halted boats between Caticlan and Boracay as well as water activities. During the year-end holidays, Lunar New Year, and Holy Week, whose dates change every year, all of Boracay gets crowded, but even then Puka Shell Beach tends to be much quieter than White Beach.

There is no lodging on Puka Shell Beach itself. Most visitors stay at Stations 1–3 on White Beach and come by e-trike, and in Boracay you may only stay at accommodation accredited by the Department of Tourism (DOT), so check accreditation when you book. If you want to stay in the quiet north, there are large resorts such as Shangri-La Boracay on the headland at the northwestern tip, also in Barangay Yapak, and a few resorts and guesthouses inside Yapak village.

The stalls and simple eateries at the beach entrance sell grilled seafood and skewers and simple Filipino meals with rice, and the stalls crack open fresh coconuts or sell fruit such as mangoes and bananas. The choice is limited, so if you plan to stay a long time, bring plenty of drinking water and snacks. For a proper meal, most people go back to White Beach for restaurants around D'Mall or paluto, where you choose seafood at D'Talipapa market and have it cooked for you.
Most stalls and eateries accept cash only. Return empty coconuts and drink bottles to the shop or take them with you; do not leave them on the beach.
Before
or after
4 PM
it is cooler and less crowded. It is best to avoid midday, when island-hopping bangkas stop by.
When chartering an e-trike, agree on the round-trip fare and return time before you go, or ask the driver to wait. Empty vehicles are hard to find around sunset.
The sand is coarse and mixed with shell fragments, so your feet may hurt after a long walk. Water shoes also make it easier to get around on the rocks.
There is little shade on the beach, so bring a hat, sunglasses, reef-safe sunscreen and a rash guard, and rent a hut if needed.
Many stalls accept cash only. Bring plenty of small bills such as
and
It is convenient to bring your own snorkel mask and a dry bag. On some days no one rents out gear.
Buy souvenirs at the entrance stalls instead of collecting them on the beach. Shell jewelry prices are negotiable, so compare a few stalls before you buy.
If you plan to visit on an island-hopping tour, check when booking that Puka Shell Beach is on the itinerary and whether island entrance fees are included.
Photos taken from the rocks at either end of the beach capture both the white sand and the sea. The water looks clearer in the morning than at midday when the sun is high.

Just a few steps from the water's edge the sea becomes deeper than chest height, and the waves and currents are stronger than at White Beach. If you are not a confident swimmer, stay where you can touch bottom, keep children within arm's reach, and do not go in on days with high waves.
In
March 2026

, a foreign tourist who was swept out to sea at a beach in Barangay Yapak and the lifeguard who went in to rescue him both died. Lifeguards cannot always watch the whole beach, so do not swim far out alone.
A Malay municipal ordinance prohibits taking white sand and pebbles from Boracay's beaches, and under the
amendment, first-time offenders face a fine of
, one to three months in prison, or both. Do not take shells or coral fragments either.
During the southwest monsoon (
June–October
) and the typhoon season (
July–October
), waves get higher and island-hopping tours may be canceled. Check the latest announcements right before any water activity.
Do not leave your phone and wallet on the sand when you go in the water; take turns watching your belongings or keep them on you in a dry bag.
Agree on prices for huts, souvenirs and e-trikes before you use them. Trash bins may be scarce, so take your trash with you.
About
15–20 minutes
by e-trike to Station 1 on White Beach, the island's main beach, famous for fine sand and paraw sailing at sunset.
The island you see across the sea from Puka Shell Beach, about
40 minutes to 1 hour
from Boracay by chartered bangka, with cliff diving and quiet white-sand beaches.
